summary: A 1933 Forest Service detection lookout was replaced in 1966 by a state timber tower; the cab is now privately owned and locked, and sources disagree on who holds the site.

facts.design: 14x14-ft DNR cab on a 40-ft timber tower (1966); original 1933 cab was L-4 on a 40-ft pole tower

access.note: Privately owned and locked per TrailChick (updated March 2026); the summit area is open to the public, the cab is not.

visit.trail_note: Road reported relatively well maintained in November 2017; snow stopped the visitor about a mile below the lookout. Cab is locked; do not climb or enter.

facts.agency: Washington Dept. of Natural Resources (NHLR administrator; other sources describe private ownership)

events.note: U.S. Forest Service detection lookout: L-4 cab on a 40-ft pole tower. All three sources give 1933.
firelookout.com lists named lookout staff from 1952 to 1962; 1953-1954 marked not staffed.
Pole tower replaced by the current 40-ft timber tower with a 14x14-ft DNR cab.
NHLR: lookout purchased by American Resources.
Paid contractor staffed the lookout about one month while Bonaparte Lookout was renovated. The chapter report calls the contractor a Forest Service contractor and does not name a firm.
Eastern Washington FFLA chapter took up local management and performed some maintenance; not described as a restoration.
Registered on the National Historic Lookout Register, January 2, 2006.
Temporarily staffed from Bonaparte during the Spur/Walker Creek Fire, after the Bonaparte lookout was evacuated.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR lists WDNR as administrator and describes a private buyer (W.R. Morrison, then American Resources in 2004). firelookout.com says ownership passed to the state, then a private party bought it in the mid-1990s. TrailChick says the lookout is privately owned as of March 2026. Kept WDNR as the agency with private ownership noted; the sources do not settle who controls the site now.
The FFLA 2005 report calls the contractor a paid Forest Service contractor; NHLR and TrailChick tie the stay to American Resources. The sources agree on the month and the Bonaparte renovation.
NHLR's Built field gives 1966 (the current tower); its description and TrailChick give 1933 for the first lookout on the site.

notes_for_editor: Brief's design L-4 describes only the 1933 cab (corrected). Brief's built 1966 is the current tower; the site's lookout dates to 1933 (corrected). Brief's 2005 'restored' is overstated: the chapter report says local management and some maintenance (corrected). Ownership is unresolved across sources: NHLR lists WDNR as administrator with private owners; firelookout.com says state then private; TrailChick says privately owned as of March 2026. Story reports the conflict rather than picking one. The washingtonlookouts.weebly.com and willhiteweb.com pages were not read beyond their indexes. Not read: the 2014-2021 staffing reports for this tower; none were needed.
